title: Supported-section kernels commute with flat pullback for locally principal support
statement: Let $u:Q\to P$ be a flat morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism], and let $D\subseteq P$ be a closed subset that is locally principal: every point has an affine neighbourhood $V$ and $a\in\mathcal O_P(V)$ with $D\cap V=V(a)$. Set $D_Q=u^{-1}D$. Let $H$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_P$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Define a submodule sheaf $K\subseteq H$ by $K(V)=\{h\in H(V):h|_{V\setminus D}=0\}$ for each open $V\subseteq P$, and define $L\subseteq u^*H$ by $L(W)=\{h\in(u^*H)(W):h|_{W\setminus D_Q}=0\}$ for each open $W\subseteq Q$, using ordinary module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. Then $K$ and $L$ are quasi-coherent, and the pulled-back inclusion $u^*(K\hookrightarrow H)$ is injective with image exactly $L$. More explicitly, on every affine pair $W\subseteq u^{-1}V$ with $D\cap V=V(a)$, write $A=\mathcal O_P(V)$, $C=\mathcal O_Q(W)$, $M=H(V)$, and $a_C$ for the image of $a$ in $C$. Let $\eta$ denote the unit of the adjunction $u^*\dashv u_*$ of [def-pc-module-pullback]. The $C$-linear maps $\Gamma_a(M)\otimes_A C\to(u^*K)(W)$ and $M\otimes_A C\to(u^*H)(W)$ given by $s\otimes c\mapsto c\,\eta(s)|_W$ are bijective, where $\Gamma_a(M)=\{m\in M:\exists n\geq0,\ a^nm=0\}=K(V)$, and they carry the map $(u^*K)(W)\to(u^*H)(W)$ to the map $\Gamma_a(M)\otimes_A C\to M\otimes_A C$ induced by inclusion. This map is injective, and its image $\Gamma_{a_C}(M\otimes_A C)$ is carried by the second bijection onto $L(W)$.

proof.text: Choose affine neighbourhoods $V$ as in the hypothesis, with equation $a$. On $V$ take the closed subscheme $E=V(a)$ and apply [lem-trf-locally-principal-supported-kernel] with $Y=T=V$ and $q=1_V$. Its supported kernel is exactly $K|_V$, since restriction to an open $V'\subseteq V$ tests vanishing on $V'\setminus D$. Thus $K|_V$ is quasi-coherent and $V\setminus E\to V$ is quasi-compact. The latter says that the complement is retrocompact on $V$. Apply [lem-trf-supported-sections-quasi-coherent] on $V$ with the finitely generated ideal $(a)$: $K(V)=\{m\in H(V):a^nm=0\text{ for some }n\geq0\}=\Gamma_a(M)$. These neighbourhoods cover $P$, so quasi-coherence of $K$ follows directly from its affine-local definition [pqf-def-coherent]. No globally defined locally principal closed subscheme with support $D$ is needed.

By [lem-pc-ringed-space-tensor-pullback-qcoh], both $u^*H$ and $u^*K$ are quasi-coherent. For an affine $W\subseteq u^{-1}V$, one has $D_Q\cap W=V(a_C)$. Indeed at $w\in W$ the local ring homomorphism $\mathcal O_{P,u(w)}\to\mathcal O_{Q,w}$ carries $a$ to the germ of $a_C$; its inverse image of the maximal ideal is the maximal ideal, so the latter germ is a nonunit exactly when the former is. Apply [lem-trf-locally-principal-supported-kernel] on $W$ with the principal closed subscheme $V(a_C)$ and the quasi-coherent module $(u^*H)|_W$. It gives quasi-coherence of $L|_W$ and quasi-compactness of its complementary open immersion. Apply [lem-trf-supported-sections-quasi-coherent] there with $(a_C)$ to obtain $L(W)=\Gamma_{a_C}((u^*H)(W))$. These affine opens cover $Q$, and hence $L$ is quasi-coherent by [pqf-def-coherent].

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] to $H$ and $K$ on this affine pair. This gives the two $C$-linear bijections $c_H:M\otimes_A C\to(u^*H)(W)$ and $c_K:\Gamma_a(M)\otimes_A C\to(u^*K)(W)$, both with formula $s\otimes c\mapsto c\,\eta(s)|_W$. Naturality for $K\hookrightarrow H$ gives $(u^*(K\hookrightarrow H))_Wc_K=c_H(\iota\otimes1_C)$, where $\iota:\Gamma_a(M)\hookrightarrow M$ is inclusion. Since $c_H$ is $C$-linear and bijective, $a_C^nx=0$ if and only if $a_C^nc_H(x)=0$; thus $c_H$ carries $\Gamma_{a_C}(M\otimes_A C)$ bijectively onto $L(W)$ by Step 2.

source.place: Tag 01I9, lemma-widetilde-pullback (1), functorial affine pullback; Tag 01IA, lemma-quasi-coherent-affine

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion], $C$ is flat over $A$. The subset $T=\Gamma_a(M)$ is a submodule: if $a^rm=0$ and $a^sn=0$, then $a^{r+s}(m+n)=0$, and $a^r(bm)=0$ for $b\in A$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] to $0\to T\xrightarrow{\iota}M\to M/T$. It follows that $\iota\otimes1_C:T\otimes_A C\to M\otimes_A C$ is injective. Every tensor in its source is a finite sum $\sum_i t_i\otimes c_i$. Choose exponents $n_i$ killing $t_i$ and put $N=\sum_i n_i$ (with $N=0$ for the empty sum). Then $a_C^N$ kills its image, by tensor balancing. Its image is therefore contained in $\Gamma_{a_C}(M\otimes_A C)$.

source.place: Tags 00HB and 00HD, definition-flat and lemma-flat; morphisms.tex Tag 01U5, lemma-flat-characterize (1)-(2)

proof.text: Conversely, take $x\in M\otimes_A C$ with $a_C^nx=0$ for some $n\geq0$. Set $T_n=\ker(a^n:M\to M)$, an $A$-submodule contained in $T$. The sequence $0\to T_n\to M\xrightarrow{a^n}M$ is exact by the definition of kernel. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact], tensoring with $C$ makes it exact at $M\otimes_A C$. On pure tensors the last map is $m\otimes c\mapsto a^nm\otimes c=m\otimes a_C^nc=a_C^n(m\otimes c)$, so its kernel contains $x$. Exactness supplies $y\in T_n\otimes_A C$ mapping to $x$. The map induced by $T_n\subseteq T$ sends $y$ to a preimage of $x$ in $T\otimes_A C$. This proves the reverse containment, and hence the claimed image equality. The argument includes $n=0$, where $x=0$ and $T_0=0$.

source.place: Tags 00HB and 00HD, definition-flat and lemma-flat, applied to the kernel of multiplication by a power

proof.text: Steps 3--5 identify the map $u^*K\to u^*H$ on every affine pair in the statement as an injection onto $L(W)$. These $W$ cover $Q$ and refine any open neighbourhood. A section in the kernel restricts to zero on this cover, and is zero by the sheaf uniqueness axiom. For a section of $L$ on any open, the local preimages in $u^*K$ exist by the affine result, agree on overlaps by this injectivity, and glue by the sheaf axiom. Its image sheaf is therefore exactly $L$, with the asserted affine formulas.

The report says the statement and stmt_deps are unchanged, and the stmt_deps (scheme, flat morphism, quasi-coherent, module pullback) match the notions the statement uses. I read Stacks properties.tex 07ZP lemma-sections-supported-on-closed-subset (1)-(3); the flat-pullback clause is not in the source, and proof_origin correctly says the argument is the agent's. Step 1: applies lem-trf-locally-principal-supported-kernel with Y=T=V, q=1 and E=V(a); its subsheaf is K|_V, and j quasi-compact gives the retrocompactness that lem-trf-supported-sections-quasi-coherent needs, so K(V)=Gamma_a(M) with J=(a). Quasi-coherence of K is affine-local (pqf-def-coherent). The text speaks of the chosen neighbourhoods V, but the same argument works for every affine V with D cap V=V(a), so this is not a gap. Step 2: D_Q cap W=V(a_C) follows because stalk maps are local; the same two nodes applied on W give L(W)=Gamma_{a_C}. Step 3: the affine-sections node gives c with exactly the item's formula c eta(s)|_W, and its naturality for the inclusion K into H gives the map; c_H is C-linear, so it carries the torsion submodule onto L(W). Step 4: C is flat over A by the affine criterion, 0->T->M->M/T stays exact so the map is injective, and the image is killed by a_C^N with N=sum n_i. Step 5: the exact sequence 0->T_n->M->M (multiplication by a^n) stays exact after tensoring, which gives the reverse containment. Step 6: injectivity, image in L and gluing are checked on a basis of affine W; this is elementary. Edge cases tested: a=0 or nilpotent, a a unit, M=0, W empty, n=0, unbounded torsion exponents, and the non-flat counterexample Z->Z/2 with a=2 (so flatness is needed and is assumed). Duplicate search: nagata power-torsion localization covers only localization; per-local-cohomology flat base change needs Noetherian rings; no node states the item.
